extracted.intended_audience: Museums (units of government or private nonprofit museums) and affiliated organizations preparing FY2024 IMLS Museums for America grant applications (U.S. jurisdictions listed)
extracted.subtask_short: IMLS Museums for America grant application
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting a Museums for America (IMLS) FY2024 grant application, including required documents, narrative, budget, performance measurement, and any conditionally required plans (digital products, conservation surveys). Applies to U.S. museums and eligible lead organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: organizational type and status
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible your organization must (1) be a unit of State, local, or tribal government or a private, nonprofit organization with tax-exempt status under the Internal Revenue Code; (2) be located in one of the specified U.S. jurisdictions (50 states, DC, certain territories and Freely Associated States); and (3) qualify as a museum using professional staff organized on a permanent basis for educational/cultural/aesthetic purposes, owning or using tangible objects, caring for them, and exhibiting them to the public on a regular basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes examples of what counts as a museum (aquariums, arboretums, botanical gardens, etc.), definition of 'using a professional staff' (at least one FTE primarily engaged in acquisition/care/exhibition), and 'exhibit to the general public' (exhibiting at least 120 days/year deemed regular). Museums inside parent organizations may apply on their own only if they meet discrete-unit criteria (segregated budget, authority to apply, function as discrete unit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: lead applicant requirement for partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: When two or more eligible institutions collaborate, one must meet all eligibility requirements, serve as lead applicant, and administer the award on behalf of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lead applicant will be programmatically, fiscally, and legally responsible for the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost share requirement (1:1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees must provide funds from non-federal sources equal to or greater than the federal award (minimum 1:1 cost share).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your project budget does not include at least 1:1 cost share, the application will be rejected from consideration. Cost share should be carefully calculated and awardees are expected to meet commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and project period constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual awards are expected to be $5,000 - $250,000; projects may run one to three years and must begin on September 1, 2024 with performance period through Aug 31, 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If total request is < $5,000 or > $250,000, application may be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission method and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted electronically through Grants.gov Workspace (or system-to-system) by 11:59 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time on November 15, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit by email or postal mail. Grants.gov generates status emails; applicants should register and submit early. Under certain disaster declarations extensions may be allowed; check guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application components and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must include all Required Documents and any Conditionally Required Documents; missing required/conditional documents will make an application incomplete and may lead to rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Table of Application Components as a checklist. IMLS will not review ineligible or incomplete applications. Attach components in the sequence listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document formats, filenames, and attachment order
rubrics_metrics.description: All application components (except SF-424S and IMLS Museum Program Information Form) must be PDF documents. Use specified file names. Attachment filenames limited to A-Z, a-z, 0-9, underscore, hyphen, space, period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach documents in the sequence listed; use all 'Attachments Form' slots first; extra components go in 'Other Attachment File(s)'. Incorrect file name characters may cause Grants.gov rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative: page limit and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Narrative is limited to seven numbered pages. Use at least 0.5-inch margins and a font size of at least eleven points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS will remove any additional pages and not send them to reviewers. Be concise and limit technical jargon and acronyms. Include references to Supporting Documents within the Narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative: organization by headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the Narrative using the section headings: Project Justification, Project Work Plan, and Project Results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the Museums for America goal and objective(s) you selected and explicitly identify them in the Narrative (see Section A2). Reviewers may visit your website listed on SF-424S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Justification content
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain which program goal/project category and objective(s) the project addresses; how it advances your museum's strategic plan; the need/problem/challenge to be addressed and how it was identified; the target group and how they were involved in planning; and the ultimate beneficiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe use of demographic information, economic circumstances, condition assessments, and other reliable data to define the need. Identify numbers for target groups and beneficiaries where reliable and defensible counts are possible; otherwise describe characteristics. Clearly state chosen program goal/objective(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Work Plan content
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the specific activities and their sequence; project risks and mitigation strategies; who will plan, implement, and manage the project; and the time, financial, personnel, and other resources required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how progress toward intended results will be tracked. Include a Schedule of Completion reflecting major activities and project dates (one page per project year recommended).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Results content
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe intended results and how they address the identified need from both perspectives of advancing knowledge/understanding and ensuring federal investment generates societal benefits; how target group knowledge/skills/behaviors/attitudes will change; products to result; sustainability of benefits; and, for Collections Stewardship and Access projects, how collections care/condition/management/access/use will improve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about long-term benefits and sustainability strategies. Tie results to the need and to measurable outcomes where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Measurement Plan requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A Performance Measurement Plan (recommended two pages) must show how you will monitor and assess performance from the perspectives of Effectiveness, Efficiency, Quality, and Timeliness for the overall project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each measure, identify what data will be collected, from what source, the method of collection, and the schedule. A sample chart and a fillable version are provided; limit to two pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measures definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS uses four performance measures: Effectiveness (extent activities contribute to intended results), Efficiency (how well resources are used and costs minimized while generating value), Quality (how well activities meet target group requirements and expectations), and Timeliness (extent tasks are completed within proposed timeframe).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must describe how they will monitor and assess these four measures in their Performance Measurement Plan (see D2c Item 7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Budget Justification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the IMLS Budget Form and provide a Budget Justification explaining each expense and the method of cost computation, including consolidated or summarized items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide vendor quotes or price lists for supplies/equipment as Supporting Documents. Identify total direct costs, how much requested from IMLS and cost share, indirect cost rate and base if included, and total project costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of Key Project Staff and Resumes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a list of only staff and consultants essential to project success (one page recommended) and resumes for each essential individual (two pages each recommended) combined into a single PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must include Project Director listed on SF-424S; if key staff cannot be identified at deadline, provide position descriptions including required qualities, experience, and education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditionally required documents: proof of nonprofit status
rubrics_metrics.description: If applying as a private nonprofit (Applicant Type code 'M'), submit a copy of the IRS letter indicating eligibility for nonprofit status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state sales tax exemption letter is not acceptable as proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditionally required documents: indirect cost rate documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: If using a federally negotiated indirect cost rate, provide a copy of the current Final Federally Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If electing the de minimis 10% MTDC rate, documentation of a negotiated rate is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditionally required documents: Digital Products Plan (if applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: If proposing to generate digital content/resources/software, submit a Digital Products Plan (two pages recommended) describing Type, Availability, Access, and Sustainability of digital products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe types and quantities of digital products, file formats, metadata, standards used, delivery strategy, infrastructure, licensing, rights assertions, privacy/cultural sensitivity handling, preservation plans, and commitment of organizational funding for curation. IMLS encourages open access and open-source licensing and participates in FADGI; include reasons for any limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditionally required documents: conservation documentation (if proposing conservation treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: If proposing conservation treatment, submit a document identifying conservation priorities and how they were established, plus detailed condition reports and/or treatment proposals for each object/specimen to be treated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports may include a Conservation Assessment for Preservation (CAP), Preservation Assistance Grant (PAG) report, prior General Conservation Survey, similar funded survey, or current Long-range Conservation Plan approved by the organization. A detailed conservation survey should precede treatment requests and should produce item-level condition reports with priority, cost, and treatment method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting Documents guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may submit a reasonable number of Supporting Documents that supplement the Narrative and help reviewers envision the project; these documents should not introduce new topics or continue Narrative answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: letters of commitment, bibliography, letters of support, images, exhibit design plans, reports from planning activities, contractor quotes, equipment specs, prior project products/evaluations, departmental plans, web links, needs assessments. Give each document a clear descriptive title on first page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable and unallowable costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may use IMLS funds and cost share only for allowable costs under IMLS and OMB cost principles (2 C.F.R. part 200 and 2 C.F.R. part 3187). Examples of allowable costs include personnel, travel for key staff, materials/supplies/equipment related to project, adaptive technologies, equipment to improve collections storage/exhibit environments, third-party costs, publication design/printing, program evaluation, training, paid internships/fellowships, indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of unallowable costs include general fundraising, contributions to endowments, general operating support, acquisition of collections, general advertising/public relations solely for promotion, construction/renovation (construction trades), social activities/entertainment, and research projects (see cited regs). Contact IMLS staff for specific questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party costs and subrecipient/contractor determination
rubrics_metrics.description: When paying third parties (partners, consultants, vendors), the applicant must determine whether each third party is a subrecipient or contractor and reflect that characterization in agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 2 C.F.R. § 200.1 definitions and 2 C.F.R. § 200.331 for determinations. IMLS funds may not be provided to federal agencies as third parties. Describe each third party by name, role, activities, cost, and whether designated subrecipient or contractor; explain costs and provide supporting documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration requirements before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting, applicants must have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), a current and active SAM registration, and an active Grants.gov registration with an approved Authorized Organization Representative (AOR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration is a multi-step process that can take weeks; do not wait until the deadline. Awardees must ensure subrecipients also have UEIs. No fee to register with SAM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment length recommendations for supplemental materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended page limits for many attachments: Organizational Profile (1 page), Strategic Plan Summary (2 pages), Schedule of Completion (1 page per project year), Performance Measurement Plan (2 pages), List of Key Project Staff (1 page), Resumes (2 pages each), Digital Products Plan (2 pages recommended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are recommendations; the Narrative 7-page limit is enforced by removing additional pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Products: availability, licensing, and access expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS encourages recipients to make works produced with IMLS support widely available and to share work products (publications, datasets, educational resources, software, digital content) through free/open-access journals and repositories whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS expects publications to be accessible without charge. Applicants should identify delivery strategy and technical infrastructure, specify licenses (e.g., Creative Commons), explain limitations, and address privacy/cultural sensitivity. IMLS reserves a royalty-free, nonexclusive, irrevocable right to reproduce or authorize use of works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Products: sustainability and preservation planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must describe how digital products will be preserved and maintained during and after the period of performance, identifying appropriate retention length for different products and addressing storage systems, shared repositories, technical documentation, migration planning, and organizational funding commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between products that require long-term preservation and those appropriate for medium- or short-term retention (e.g., drafts, social media). Costs for publication/sharing may be charged before closeout if not incurred during the award period (2 C.F.R. § 200.461).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservation survey types and required report contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for three survey types: General Conservation Survey, Detailed Conservation Survey, and Environmental Survey, each with specific purposes and required report contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General survey should include executive summary, general information, goals, collections overview and condition, building/facilities condition, climate/environment descriptions, staffing/training needs, and prioritized recommendations. Detailed survey should produce item-level condition reports with treatment priority, cost, and method and precede treatment grants. Environmental survey should assess temperature, RH, light, identify problems, set priorities, design solutions, develop monitoring, and map collections (for living plants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-federal entities must follow IMLS conflict of interest policies for federal awards: disclose any potential conflict in writing to an IMLS Program Officer immediately (applicants and awardees) and maintain written standards of conduct covering conflicts of interest for employees involved in selection, award, and administration of subawards and contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees with a real or apparent conflict (financial or tangible benefit to them/close relations) may not participate in selection/award/administration. Organizational conflicts of interest (due to parent/affiliate/subsidiary relationships) must also be addressed with written standards.
